meta.title: Directive 2012/13/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 May 2012 on the right to information in criminal proceedings

items.text: This Directive lays down rules concerning the right to information of suspects or accused persons, relating to their rights in criminal proceedings and to the accusation against them. It also lays down rules concerning the right to information of persons subject to a European Arrest Warrant relating to their rights.

Where the law of a Member State provides for the imposition of a sanction regarding minor offences by an authority other than a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters, and the imposition of such a sanction may be appealed to such a court, this Directive shall apply only to the proceedings before that court, following such an appeal.
items.comment:
Article 318 CCP regulates the waiver of prosecution solution. This can be decided by the public prosecutor in cases where the law stipulates the penalty of the fine or the punishment of imprisonment for a maximum of 7 years, and when there is no public interest in the prosecution. The solution of the prosecutor must be checked for both legality and opportunity by the preliminary chamber judge (see Article 318 para. 12 et seq., amended by Emergency Ordinance no. 18/2016, following decision no. 23/2016 of the Constitutional Court).

Therefore, in front of the court (in this case the preliminary chamber judge), the general standards regarding right of information apply. In addition, if the person aquired the status of suspect or accused during the investigation phase, all the general standards are hence incident.


As a general rule - with no exceptions at this time - we can say that, in Romanian law, the competence for imposing sanctions - even in relation to relatively minor offences - belongs only to courts with jurisdiction in criminal matters.

The rights of the accused person


During the criminal trial, the accused person has the following rights:

a) the right not to give any statement during the criminal trial, drawing attention to the fact that if he refuses to give statements he will not suffer any adverse consequences, and if he gives statements they will be able to be used as evidence against him;

a1) the right to be informed about the deed for which it is investigated and its legal status;

b) the right to consult the file, according to the law;

c) the right to have a lawyer elected, and if he does not designate one, in the cases of compulsory assistance, the right to be appointed a lawyer ex officio;

d) the right to propose the administration of evidence under the conditions provided by law, to raise exceptions and to draw conclusions;

e) the right to make any other requests related to solving the criminal and civil side of the case;

f) the right to benefit free of charge of an interpreter when he does not understand, express himself well or cannot communicate in Romanian;

g) the right to call a mediator, in the cases allowed by law;

g1) the right to be informed about his rights;

h) other rights provided by law.

Rights of the suspect


The suspect has the rights provided by law for the accused person, unless the law provides otherwise.

provisions.textEn:
C. The right to consult the file, according to the law


You can consult your file under the conditions provided by law, personally or through a lawyer. This means that you can study the records of the file, write down data or information from the file and get photocopies (xerox copies) at your expence.

The date and duration of the consultation, during the criminal investigation, will be determined by the prosecutor.

During the criminal prosecution, the prosecutor may reasonably restrict the consultation of the file, for good reasons. If you are an accused person, this restriction may not last more than 10 days.

In all cases, the lawyer who assists or represents you may not be restricted from consulting your statements.

J. The right to inform another person about the arrest or detention / information of the consulate or embassy of your country


Immediately after taking the detention or house arrest, you have the right to personally announce or request the judicial body that has ordered the measure to notify a member of your family or another person of your choice about the measure that was taken and the location (detention facility) where you are placed.

If the pre-trial arrest (preventive arrest measure) has been ordered regarding you:

- the judge will immediately inform a member of your family or another person nominated by you;

- as soon as you are taken to a place of detention, you have the right to personally inform or ask the administration of the place of detention to inform a family member or other person of your choice about the place where you are.

In the case of detention as well as preventive arrest, if you are moved to another place of detention, you also have the right to personally inform or ask the administration of the place of detention to inform a family member or other chosen person. by you on the place where you were transferred.

In the case of custody (retention) and pre-trial detention, the right to personally announce these persons may be denied only for sound reasons, which are recorded in the minutes.

If you are not a Romanian citisen, you have the right to inform or ask the police or prosecutor (if you are detained) or the judge or court (if you are preventive arrested or home arrested) to inform the diplomatic mission or consular post of the state whose city you are you.

If you do not want to notify the authorities in your country, you can inform or request that information be made to an an international humanitarian organisation.

Also, if you are a refugee or, for any other reason, you are under the protection of an international organisation, you can inform or request that notification is made to its representation.

provisions.textEn:
L. Period of deprivation of liberty


You can be retained (taken into custody) by the police officer or prosecutor for up to 24 hours. This period does not include the time strictly necessary to lead at the headquarters of the judiciary nor the term of 8 hours if you were brought with a warrant.

The measure of house arrest and the measure of preventive arrest can be taken against you, both during the criminal investigation, as well as during the preliminary chamber procedure and during the trial, for a period of 30 days.

During the criminal prosecution this period may be extended by the judge of rights and freedoms, each extension not exceeding 30 days. The maximum duration of the measure of house arrest or preventive arrest, during the criminal investigation, is 180 days.

During the preliminary chamber procedure and the trial, the judge can maintain the measure after the expiration of 30 days.

During the trial in the first instance, the total duration of the house arrest or the preventive arrest may not be more than half the maximum penalty provided in the law for the offence for which you are tried. In all cases, the duration of the house arrest or the preventive arrest at first instance may not exceed 5 years.

provisions.textEn:
M. The right to challenge the measure ordered


- If you are detained:

If you have been detained by the police, you have the right to challenge the measure to the prosecutor who oversees the prosecution, before the expiration of its duration. The prosecutor will rule immediately.

If you have been detained by the prosecutor, you can challenge the measure to the first prosecutor of the prosecutor's office or, as the case may be, to the superior hierarchical prosecutor. It will be pronounced immediately.

- If you are pre-trial arrested or at home, during the criminal prosecution or during the preliminary chamber procedure, you can file an appeal within 48 hours after the ruling, if you were present at the hearing, or since the measure was communicated, if you were not present at the hearing.

You will file the appeal with the judge of rights and freedoms or with the preliminary chamber judge who has taken the preventive arrest measure or at your home.

If you are house (home) arrested during the trial:

You can file an appeal within 48 hours of the ruling (if you were present at the hearing) or since the measure was communicated to you, if you were not present at the hearing.

You will file the appeal with the court that ordered the measure.

N. Right to request the revocation or replacement of the measure of house arrest or preventive arrest


You have the right to request the revocation of the deprivation of liberty measure, if you consider that the grounds that caused it or new circumstances that resulted in the illegality of the measure have ceased, as well as the right to request the replacement of the liberty measure with another easier preventive measure.

(1) If, after the commencement of the criminal prosecution, the criminal prosecution body finds new facts, data on the participation of other persons or circumstances, which may lead to the change of the legal classification of the deed, it orders the extension of the criminal prosecution or the change of the legal classification .

The sole purpose of this model is to assist national authorities in drawing up their Letter of Rights at national level. Member States are not bound to use this model. When preparing their Letter of Rights, Member States may amend this model in order to align it with their national rules and add further useful information. The Member State’s Letter of Rights must be given upon arrest or detention. This however does not prevent Member States from providing suspects or accused persons with written information in other situations during criminal proceedings.


A. ASSISTANCE OF A LAWYER/ENTITLEMENT TO LEGAL AID


You have the right to speak confidentially to a lawyer. A lawyer is independent from the police. Ask the police if you need help to get in contact with a lawyer, the police shall help you. In certain cases the assistance may be free of charge. Ask the police for more information.


B. INFORMATION ABOUT THE ACCUSATION


You have the right to know why you have been arrested or detained and what you are suspected or accused of having done.


C. INTERPRETATION AND TRANSLATION


If you do not speak or understand the language spoken by the police or other competent authorities, you have the right to be assisted by an interpreter, free of charge. The interpreter may help you to talk to your lawyer and must keep the content of that communication confidential. You have the right to translation of at least the relevant passages of essential documents, including any order by a judge allowing your arrest or keeping you in custody, any charge or indictment and any judgment. You may in some circumstances be provided with an oral translation or summary.


D. RIGHT TO REMAIN SILENT


While questioned by the police or other competent authorities, you do not have to answer questions about the alleged offence. Your lawyer can help you to decide on that.


E. ACCESS TO DOCUMENTS


When you are arrested and detained, you (or your lawyer) have the right to access essential documents you need to challenge the arrest or detention. If your case goes to court, you (or your lawyer) have the right to access the material evidence for or against you.


F. INFORMING SOMEONE ELSE ABOUT YOUR ARREST OR DETENTION/INFORMING YOUR CONSULATE OR EMBASSY


When you are arrested or detained, you should tell the police if you want someone to be informed of your detention, for example a family member or your employer. In certain cases the right to inform another person of your detention may be temporarily restricted. In such cases the police will inform you of this.


If you are a foreigner, tell the police if you want your consular authority or embassy to be informed of your detention. Please also tell the police if you want to contact an official of your consular authority or embassy.


G. URGENT MEDICAL ASSISTANCE


When you are arrested or detained, you have the right to urgent medical assistance. Please let the police know if you are in need of such assistance.


H. PERIOD OF DEPRIVATION OF LIBERTY


After your arrest you may be deprived of liberty or detained for a maximum period of … [fill in applicable number of hours/days]. At the end of that period you must either be released or be heard by a judge who will decide on your further detention. Ask your lawyer or the judge for information about the possibility to challenge your arrest, to review the detention or to ask for provisional release.

provisions.textEn:
Information on the rights of the person deprived of liberty in the criminal trial, having the following content:

"If the measure of detention, house arrest or preventive arrest has been ordered against you, you have the following rights:

A. The right not to make any statement during the criminal trial

Refusal to give statements will not be construed as a guilty plea and will not have any other adverse consequences on you.

If you give statements, they may be used as evidence against you.

B. The right to be informed of the act for which you are arrested / detained and of its legal status

C. The right to consult the file, according to the law

You can consult your file under the conditions provided by law, personally or through a lawyer. This means that you can study the records of the file, write down data or information from the file and get photocopies (xerox copies) at your expense.

The date and duration of the consultation, during the criminal investigation, will be determined by the prosecutor.

During the criminal prosecution, the prosecutor may reasonably restrict the consultation of the file, for good reasons. If you are guilty, this restriction may not last more than 10 days.

In all cases, the lawyer who assists or represents you may not be restricted from consulting your statements.

D. The right to have a lawyer elected

You have the right to be assisted and represented by a lawyer chosen and paid by you.

In all cases where the presence of the lawyer is obligatory, if you do not want to appoint yourself an elected lawyer, you will be assigned an ex officio lawyer.

If you are given legal assistance ex officio, it is free.

E. The right to propose the administration of evidence under the conditions provided by law, to raise exceptions and to draw conclusions

You can propose the administration of evidence (for example, hearing of persons, conducting expertise, submitting documents or evidence), you can raise exceptions (for example, exceptions of incompetence, exceptions regarding the legality of the court referral, the legality of administering the evidence and of the acts performed by the criminal prosecution bodies - in the preliminary chamber procedure, exceptions of unconstitutionality) and you can draw conclusions by expressing your point of view on all aspects of the case.

F. The right to make any other requests during the criminal trial, related to solving the criminal and civil side of the case

You can make any other requests that contribute to the resolution of your case (for example, requests for recusal, requests for the necessary facilities to prepare for effective defense, requests to change the legal framework).

G. The right to have an interpreter free of charge

If you do not speak or understand the language spoken by the authorities, you have the right to have an interpreter free of charge, who will help you communicate with the authorities, become aware of the parts of the file, speak and make conclusions in court.

If you do not speak or understand the language spoken by the authorities, you have the right to be informed of a written translation of the indictment, as well as of the minutes and court decision.

In cases where legal aid is required, the interpreter can help you for free to communicate with your lawyer.

You have the right to be informed in the language you understand the reasons for which you were detained / arrested at home / preventively arrested.

H. The right to call a mediator

In cases permitted by law, you have the right to use the mediation procedure to resolve the conflict.

You cannot be forced to use mediation if you do not want to.

I. The right to be informed about your rights

You have the right for the judicial bodies (police, prosecutor, judge) to communicate to you what your rights are during the criminal prosecution and the trial.

J. The right to inform another person about the arrest or detention / information of the consulate or embassy of your country

Immediately after taking the detention or arrest at home, you have the right to personally announce or request the judicial body that has ordered the measure to notify a member of your family or another person of your choice about the measure that was taken and where you are situated.

If the preventive arrest measure has been taken on you:

- the judge will immediately inform a member of your family or another person designated by you;

- as soon as you are taken to a place of detention, you have the right to personally announce or ask the administration of the place of detention to notify a family member or other person of your choice about the place where you are.

In the case of detention as well as preventive arrest, if you are moved to another place of detention, you also have the right to personally announce or ask the administration of the place of detention to notify a family member or other chosen person. by you on the place where you were transferred.

In the case of pre-trial detention and detention, the right to personally announce these persons may be denied only for sound reasons, which are recorded in the minutes.

If you are not a Romanian citizen, you have the right to notify or ask the police or prosecutor (if you are detained) or the judge or court (if you are preventively arrested or arrested at home) to announce the diplomatic mission or consular post of the state whose city you are you.

If you do not want to notify the authorities in your country, you can announce or request the announcement of an international humanitarian organization.

Also, if you are a refugee or, for any other reason, under the protection of an international organization, you can announce or request the announcement of its representation.

K. The right to emergency medical care

If you are arrested or detained, you are entitled to emergency medical care. Please tell the judicial body if you need such assistance.

L. Period of deprivation of liberty

You can be detained by the police officer or prosecutor for up to 24 hours. During the detention does not include the time strictly necessary to lead at the headquarters of the judiciary, nor the term of 8 hours if you were brought with a warrant.

The measure of house arrest and the measure of preventive arrest can be taken against you, both during the criminal investigation, as well as during the preliminary chamber procedure and during the trial, for a period of 30 days.

During the criminal prosecution this period may be extended by the judge of rights and freedoms, each extension not exceeding 30 days. The maximum duration of the measure of house arrest or preventive arrest, during the criminal investigation, is 180 days.

During the preliminary chamber procedure and the trial, the judge can maintain the measure after the expiration of 30 days.

During the trial in the first instance, the total duration of the house arrest or the preventive arrest may not be more than half the maximum penalty provided in the law for the offense for which you are tried. In all cases, the duration of the house arrest or the preventive arrest at first instance may not exceed 5 years.

M. The right to challenge the measure ordered

- If you are detained:

If you have been detained by the police, you have the right to challenge the measure to the prosecutor who oversees the prosecution, before the expiration of its duration. The prosecutor will rule immediately.

If you have been detained by the prosecutor, you can challenge the measure to the first prosecutor of the prosecutor's office or, as the case may be, to the superior hierarchical prosecutor. It will be pronounced immediately.

- If you are arrested pre-emptively or at home, during the criminal prosecution or during the preliminary court procedure, you can file an appeal within 48 hours after the ruling, if you were present at the hearing, or since the measure was communicated, if you were not present at the hearing.

You will file the appeal with the judge of rights and freedoms or the preliminary chamber judge who has taken the preventive arrest measure or at your home.

If you are arrested pre-emptively or at home during the trial:

You can file an appeal within 48 hours of the ruling (if you were present at the hearing) or since the measure was communicated to you, if you were not present at the hearing.

You will file the appeal with the court that ordered the measure.

N. Right to request the revocation or replacement of the measure of house arrest or preventive arrest

You have the right to request the revocation of the deprivation of liberty measure, if you consider that the grounds that caused it or new circumstances that resulted in the illegality of the measure have ceased, as well as the right to request the replacement of the liberty measure with another easier preventive measure.

O. The right to challenge the duration of the criminal trial

If the activity of criminal prosecution or trial is not carried out within a reasonable time, you have the right to file an appeal requesting the speeding up of the procedure.

The appeal may be filed after at least one year after the commencement of the prosecution (for the cases in the course of the criminal prosecution), after at least one year after the trial (for the cases during the trial in the first instance) and after at least 6 months from the notification of the court with an appeal (for the cases in the ordinary or extraordinary appeals) ”.

provisions.textEn:
Information on the rights of the person deprived of liberty based on a European arrest warrant

"If you are deprived of liberty in the process of executing a European arrest warrant, you have the following rights:

A. The right to be informed about the content of the European arrest warrant

You have the right to be informed, in the language you understand, of the reasons for the detention and the content of the European arrest warrant.

You have the right to be handed a copy of the European arrest warrant and its translation.

B. The right to remain silent

You are not required to make a statement before the prosecutor or judge. A lawyer can also advise you on the Romanian law applicable to the European arrest warrant and can help you decide whether or not to answer questions.

C. The right to be assisted by a lawyer

You have the right to be assisted by a lawyer, elected or appointed ex officio. If you do not have the opportunity to hire an elected lawyer, the police, prosecutor or judge before whom you will be presented must inform you how you can get free legal assistance.

The measure of provisional detention or detention may be taken only after your hearing in the presence of the lawyer.

If you are given legal assistance ex officio, it is free.

The lawyer is independent of the police, prosecutor and judge bodies and will not disclose, without your consent, any information that you communicate. You have the right to speak with a lawyer under confidentiality.

D. The right to interpretation and translation

If you do not speak or understand the language spoken by the Romanian authorities, you have the right to have a free interpreter. The interpreter will help you to communicate with your lawyer and the Romanian authorities, to speak, to give statements and to make conclusions in court.

E. The right to notify someone that you have been deprived of liberty

You have the right to ask the Romanian authorities to be informed about the action taken by a family member or other person designated by you. Both the request and the acknowledgment are recorded in a report.

Exceptionally, if the Romanian prosecutor considers that this would affect the execution of the European arrest warrant issued against you, he has the right to refuse your request.

F. For foreign nationals: The right to inform the embassy of your country

If you are a foreigner, you can ask the judicial authorities to inform your country's embassy or consular service about your detention and place of detention. The judicial authorities should help you if you want to talk to officials of the embassy or consular service of your country.

You have the right to write to your country's embassy or consular service. If you do not know the address, the judicial authorities should help you. The embassy or consular service can help you find a lawyer.

G. The right to agree with your teaching in Romania

You have the right to declare before the Romanian court that you give up the benefits that the Romanian law can confer on you against the European arrest warrant and that you consent to being handed over to the competent authorities of the requesting State.

You have to keep in mind that once you have agreed to surrender you no longer have the opportunity to revert to your decision, consent to surrender is irrevocable.

H. The right to oppose teaching

If you do not agree with your surrender to the issuing judicial authority, you have the right to a hearing before the executing judicial authority, a hearing that is limited to the recording of your position against the existence of one of the compulsory or optional reasons for non-execution, as well as any objections. in terms of identity.

I. The specialty rule

The person surrendered as an effect of the European arrest warrant shall not be prosecuted, prosecuted, deprived of liberty, or subject to any other restriction of liberty, for any fact prior to surrender, other than that which motivated the European arrest warrant. A lawyer can help and advise you in this regard.

You have the right to declare before the Romanian court that you give up the benefits that the specialty rule can confer. The consent is irrevocable.

J. The right to emergency medical care

If you are deprived of liberty, you are entitled to emergency medical care. Please notify the judicial body if you need such assistance.

K. Appeals

You have the right to appeal against the termination of the order to take, maintain, replace or stop the provisional arrest within 24 hours of the ruling.

Also, if your surrender has been ordered, you have the right to appeal against the judgment of the court, within 5 days of the ruling, unless you have consented to the surrender, when the judgment is final.

L. Total length of arrest

The total duration of the arrest, until the actual surrender to the issuing State, may not exceed 180 days ”.
